messages:
maria: Heads-up — nightly candidate-kernel sweep flagged a perf regression on Ampere for mid-seqlen workloads (seqlen 256-512). Starting thread to collect traces and decide rollback or tweak heuristics. :eyes:

jon: ugh, details? is it a kernel selection change or something in batching?

maria: Looks like kernel_selector picked kernel 'k12a-opt' over 'k9b-vec' for a handful of traces. End-to-end p50 latency up ~18% on microbench harness. KV cache hit% dropped ~6% in the same runs.

priya: Can you paste the CI diff / perfbot output?

maria: sure — relevant excerpt from the nightly summary:

```
perf-bot: run 2026-06-12T02:00Z (suite: candidate-kernels-nightly)
- workload: midseq-am1 (seqlen distribution: 64@10%, 256@70%, 1024@20%)
- baseline kernel: k9b-vec
- candidate kernel: k12a-opt
- p50 latency: baseline 9.8ms -> candidate 11.6ms (+18.4%)
- p95 latency: baseline 32ms -> candidate 35ms (+9.3%)
- tokens/sec: baseline 1250 -> candidate 1180 (-5.6%)
- kv-cache hit: baseline 83% -> candidate 77% (-6pp)
- batching effective batch size: baseline 12.4 -> candidate 11.1
- artifacts: https://redwood.ci/runs/12345/logs
```

jon: The drop in effective batching is suspicious — maybe kernel k12a-opt forces a different scheduling path that reduces packable requests. Any scheduler logs?

maria: attached the scheduler snippet from the run (trimmed):

```
[2026-06-12T02:00:12Z] scheduler: pick_path ampere_midseq -> path=seqlen-256-hot (heuristic v2)
[2026-06-12T02:00:12Z] selector: chosen_kernel=k12a-opt (estimate_throughput=1100 tps)
[2026-06-12T02:00:12Z] batcher: built_batch_size=8 (requests dropped to fit kernel alignment)
[2026-06-12T02:00:12Z] kvcache: evict_policy=LRU window=50 requests, hit_rate_est=0.78
```

wei: interesting — k12a-opt has a 32-byte alignment constraint that can fragment batching when mix of short and mid sequences present. That would explain effective batch size drop. Kernel autotune probably preferred it for long sequences but mis-picked for this mixed distribution.

priya: can we repro locally with the same seq distro and check microprobe results? If the autotuner's cost model underestimates fragmentation overhead we should update the model.

maria: repro steps I used:
```
# run harness workload with same mix
./microbench --model gptx --arch ampere --seq-dist 64:10,256:70,1024:20 --kernel-candidates k9b-vec,k12a-opt --runs 300
```
Output snippet (median of 5 runs):
```
k9b-vec -> p50 9.9ms, eff_batch 12.3, kv_hit 0.83
k12a-opt -> p50 11.4ms, eff_batch 11.0, kv_hit 0.77
```

jon: thanks. Two quick mitigations: (1) revert the kernel gating change in CI so candidate isn't auto-promoted until we fix cost model, (2) add a microprobe that measures alignment-induced fragmentation cost and feeds autotuner.

perf-bot: ACTIONS proposed by autopilot: revert-gate=false, add-probe=seq-align-frag, notify=#eng-runtime. Confirm?

maria: I vote revert-gate=true for now. We shouldn't let this candidate influence traffic until the autotuner accounts for batching fragmentation.

priya: +1. I'll open a PR to add the seq-align-frag probe and modify the autotune cost function (weight fragmentation penalty). Also adding a rule: if effective batch size drops >7% relative to baseline, mark candidate as regression automatically.

wei: for triage — useful to capture KV cache eviction churn as well. If kernel changes cause different per-token emplace timing, it can shift KV lifetimes. I'll add an instrumentation point in the harness to record per-request KV lifetimes (histogram).

jon: timeline? can we get a quick patch in tonight's nightly and re-run?

priya: I'll submit PR now (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7892) with the new probe and the model fix. If CI green, schedule an extra sweep on the same dataset.

maria: thanks. I'll flip the gating flag in CI to block k12a-opt until the sweep completes. Leaving this thread open for results. :thumbsup:
